turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have twenty minutes, Hale, and a client call at 4:40. Owen found out about a zero from his phone, in the middle of class. Why didn't anyone call me first?
"Upset" is your word, Hale, and it doesn't answer me. Your own procedure says a parent is contacted before any mark is entered. Did anyone call me, yes or no?
But I'm not changing the grade.
"Not changing" it, on what basis? Who decided, and was Owen heard before the zero went in? I'm writing down that you won't tell me.
I'm still not changing it. Keep going if you like.

"Keep going if you like." Fine, I'll keep going, and I'll be writing it all down. You've given me a zero and no reason, and you still haven't said what you're basing it on. If that's all you have, I'm going to the principal's office when we're done.
You can say it ten more ways. The answer is no.

"The answer is no" isn't a reason, Hale, it's a position. Your own procedure says software alone doesn't establish a concern, and that a parent is called before a mark goes in. Unless you have something else to show me, this conversation moves upstairs.
